business_problem: SumUp's centralized data platform had become a bottleneck, leaving teams waiting for pipelines, reports, and analytics while siloed systems made it difficult to provide merchants with better real-time products and decisions at global scale.
solution_summary: SumUp used Confluent Cloud to implement a data-mesh-oriented event architecture that decentralizes data ownership and turns siloed operational information into reusable streaming data products. The managed platform lets teams publish and consume standardized streams without waiting on a central platform group to build every new pipeline. Kafka Connect and Schema Registry support consistent interfaces and data quality, while Confluent Cloud runs across on-premises and AWS-hosted environments and fits into SumUp's microservices architecture backed by Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. Internal teams now publish streams directly to the shared platform, and downstream groups use them for reporting, CRM, analytics, banking services, and machine learning use cases. This shifted the platform team away from pipeline firefighting toward governance, self-service enablement, and higher-value data product work.

solution_components.name: Confluent Cloud
solution_components.role: Provides SumUp's shared managed streaming platform for publishing, governing, and consuming data products.

solution_components.name: Kafka Connect
solution_components.role: Helps SumUp standardize streaming data pipelines between source systems and downstream end systems.

solution_components.name: Schema Registry
solution_components.role: Maintains consistent event contracts and data quality across independently owned streams.

data_flow: Teams publish transaction, CRM, analytics, and operational data streams into Confluent Cloud, where standardized contracts and pipelines make the data reusable for downstream reporting, customer-facing applications, risk models, and other self-service consumers across the business.
business_outcome: SumUp reduced data-team bottlenecks, gave more than 20 internal teams self-service access to trusted streams, and accelerated customer-facing analytics, CRM, and machine-learning work without growing infrastructure overhead.
metrics: a handful of projects per quarter
